flash-flood: A flash flood is a sudden pulse of runoff. Steep or already-wet ground can shed rain fast. That is the same family of idea as slope and travel time — not a different science.
snowmelt: Snowmelt can become runoff when water is released on a slope. Gravity still pulls it downhill. I do not know your local forecast.
local: I do not know where you live. Anywhere rain or melt hits sloping ground, water can run off. Cedar Hollow is the case in front of you.
flat: If the hill were flat, the same water would usually take longer. Check that on the table if you want the number — I will not invent a flat-hill time you did not run.
gravity: Gravity pulls water downhill everywhere. Slope changes how quickly that happens. Direction still follows the fall of the land.
